result:
I re-derived everything from the sources rather than trusting the worker's extractions: re-extracted all three PDFs with pymupdf into my own directory, re-read the xlsx merge ranges, and checked every quotation and every number against my own text.

**Most of the submission holds up.** All three citations are correct (Denning's folios 323–333 and the "Volume 11 / Number 5 / May, 1968" footers; Mach's `©…/87/1000-0031` and folios 31–39; the superpages pp. 89–104 the worker flagged as inferred is confirmed by the USENIX record). Every number in the Results table is real — Table 2's `All`-vs-`4MB` columns, 18/35 and 10/35, 7.2 of 8.9 pp, Mach's 41/145 ms fork and the 19 s vs 1:16 that makes the 4:1 margin, eq. (5), eq. (10), the lσ/N sampling skew and the appendix's nτ correction. Nothing fabricated. R5/R4/R3 clean, lint exits 0, the fragment compiles with zero warnings and renders legibly.

**Three major defects, all the same R9 class the brief warned about** — the answer asserts absences the papers contradict inside the quoted passage:

- `answer.tex:54` — "the sole empirical support **anywhere**" is false. Denning's §2 invokes Fine et al. and Varian & Coffman's experiments twice and Belady's comparison. The real point (no experiment of his own tests the four-policy ranking) survives; the word "anywhere" has to go.
- `answer.tex:107` — "we are told **only** that such faults are 'rare enough in normal application programs'". The sentence continues "…**that Mach is able to outperform a version of UNIX (IBM ACIS 4.2a) on the RT**". The quote is cut exactly where the paper supplies its justification.
- `answer.tex:113` — "**and then leaves it there**". R9 names this phrasing specifically; §3.5 says Mach garbage-collects shadow objects, and the next sentence carries the discussion into the locking rules. Notably, `submission.md` claims the answer deliberately avoids this framing — the shipped text does the opposite.

Three minor items: a silently re-capitalised quote whose verifier checks a *different* string than the one shipped, τ≈2T stated as Denning's recommendation when the paper says "comparable to T" with 2T as a 50%-tolerance example, and the SHA-1 rejection cited at "up to 15%" while omitting the 60% worst case from the same passage.

Length (1464 words vs 1200–1350, 8.4% over) is inside R8's 25% threshold — noted, not a defect. All six fixes are single-clause rewrites.

Checklist written to `validators/p4/checklist.md`.

Sources: [USENIX biblio](https://www.usenix.org/biblio-10146), [OSDI '02 program](https://usenix.org/conference/osdi-02/practical-transparent-operating-system-support-superpages)

VERDICT: FAIL
